newsitem.title: USA: Ralston meets Cohen on adultery controversy.
newsitem.headline: Ralston meets Cohen on adultery controversy.

text.p: Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston met with Defense Secretary William Cohen on Monday amid expectation that Ralston might withdraw from consideration for the nation's top military job over an adulterous affair he had years ago.

Ralston, 53, made no immediate comment as he left Cohen's Pentagon office after the meeting to discuss a major controversy that erupted last week over Cohen's consideration of Ralston to become chairman of the U.S. military Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Army Gen. John Shalikashvili, whom Ralston had been favored to succeed in the top military job, meanwhile told reporters he would not consider delaying his Sept. 30 retirement to remain in the post for another two years.

Setting off a heated controversy, Cohen and the White House said last week that Ralston remained high in the running despite his admission that he had an adulterous affair while separated from his first wife 13 years ago. They subsequently divorced.

But members of Congress quickly raised questions about the fairness of the military's application of rules on adultery and have warned that the Senate might reject Ralston if he were to be nominated by President Bill Clinton to become the nation's new senior officer.

Cohen said last week that Ralston's previous affair had not threatened "the good order and discipline" of the military. But that comment came only weeks after the Air Force forced Lt. Kelly Flinn, its first woman bomber pilot, to resign to avoid a court-martial on charges of adultery, fraternization, lying and failure to obey orders.
